name: Licensure, registration, and credentialing
one_line: The organizational situation of proving, repeatedly and to several different bodies, that the holder is permitted to treat patients: statutory registration and revalidation, hospital privileging, payer or panel enrolment, scope-of-practice authorisations, and the continuing-education evidence those cycles consume. Absorbs the legacy row med.clinician-cme - CME is the evidence a registration requires, not a separate world. Gist-level placeholder (J-IND); it writes NO field rows, because the clinical_practice schema declares none.

deterministic: PRECONDITION: every entry is a DETECTION signal, never an extraction licence - this template's schema declares no field rows. “Privacy policy must be enforced before content reaches any model or external connector.”

a statutory-registration structure: an issuing health regulator matched at a word boundary against R4's gazetteer content, beside a labelled registration-number slot, a licence-status slot, and a validity or renewal window. “It should use word-boundary matching rather than substring matching.” R4 owns the gazetteer; this row writes no names and no regex.

a privileging or credentialing-application structure: a hospital or facility credentialing office as the addressee, a labelled requested-privileges or scope list, a primary-source-verification section, and an attestation-and-signature block. The requested-privileges list is the discriminating structure - an employment application does not carry one.
a payer or panel enrolment structure: a labelled provider-identifier slot beside an effective-date slot and a participation or network designation.

a revalidation or appraisal structure: a labelled cycle window, an appraiser slot, and required-evidence sections (continuing education, audit, feedback, reflective practice) - a bundle assembled to a specification rather than a single certificate.

a continuing-education structure: an accrediting body, an activity title, a credit-type designation, and a completion date, in a labelled certificate zone or a repeated log-row shape. “Tables matter because resumes, forms, applications, invoices, and administrative documents often place their most useful information in cells rather than body paragraphs.”

an archive whose manifest names a portfolio or credentialing bundle with requirement-partitioned member paths, read from the manifest alone - “the normal scan should never extract archive contents to the filesystem”.

a caseload, logbook, or procedure-numbers return submitted AS credentialing evidence - the one place this row touches patient-identifying material directly, and the reason it sits on this schema rather than only on career.
needs_llm: PRECONDITION: a credentialing bundle routinely carries an identity document, a CV, references, and case logs, so a model step runs after P7 and under the user's policy. “Protected material should not be included in cloud-model prompts by default, should not display raw content in general group summaries, and should not be moved automatically without a user policy that explicitly permits it.”

separating a licence to PRACTISE from an academic qualification, an employer-internal competency sign-off, a training completion certificate, and a professional-society membership card - all of which carry an issuing body, a name, a number, and a date.

a purpose-coherent credentialing packet whose members are individually unremarkable and whose only shared property is the submission it was assembled for. “The documents are content-incoherent but purpose-coherent.”

whether a status or disciplinary notice concerns the holder or another practitioner named in the same correspondence. The model must abstain rather than assert: “A model that cannot cite sufficient evidence must return unknown.”

a registration document from a jurisdiction whose body names and document vocabulary the deterministic catalogue does not cover - and jurisdiction is a VALUE here, never a field and never a dimension (D4).
never_alone: a certificate layout alone - a border, a seal, a signature line, a name, and a date describe a course certificate, an award, a membership card, and a licence identically. This is the tempting false file for this row.
a number-shaped token alone read as a registration number, and a bare 4-digit number read as a validity year or a cycle year.

a regulator, college, society, or hospital gazetteer hit alone. 00 states the multi-role problem for a university - “A university name alone should not create a group because Columbia can appear as an authoring school, course provider, target institution, employer, research venue, or merely a cited organization.” - and a professional body appears as issuer, employer, examiner, publisher, and conference host by the same logic (provenance: inference).
a clinician title or post-nominal alone.
source_type or extension alone. 00: “treat the file extension as a routing signal rather than an assumption about meaning”
a parent folder named Credentials, Licences, or CPD alone.
membership in a download session that pulled a portfolio's attachments at once - “A session should never be treated as proof of topic”
the words revalidation, privileges, or credentialing in a guidance document or a policy PDF, which are ABOUT the process and are not the holder's own evidence.

hospital privileging application or grant of privileges
case log, logbook, or procedure-numbers return
renewal notice, fee receipt, or lapse warning
grouping_reasons: one credentialing submission: everything assembled for one body on one occasion, purpose-coherent while its members are content-incoherent - “The documents are content-incoherent but purpose-coherent.”
one registration or revalidation cycle across its notices, evidence, and outcome.
one credential's lifecycle: grant, renewals, and lapse or restriction, joined by an exact identifier rather than by similar filenames.
one repeatedly re-downloaded portfolio export, joined by duplicate_family and version_family rather than by any professional fact.
no group at all is a valid outcome; a single certificate with no cycle around it is a standalone durable record.

template.why: Empty by binding contract. clinical_practice declares no fields, so no dimension can branch (D1 as narrowed, _CONTRACT rules 10 and 15, PR-6); and career.credentials-licenses, the nearest neighbour, is empty for exactly the same reason on the career placeholder. Unlike the chart and case-conference rows, the privacy objection here is weaker rather than absent - most of this material is about the HOLDER, and a branch named for a credential or a cycle discloses only the holder's own professional standing. The exception is real and is why this row sits on this schema: a credentialing bundle can carry case logs and audit returns about patients, and 00 names credentials in the protected-records definition - “Protected Records may represent sensitive isolated material such as passport scans, medical documents, account statements, visas, legal forms, or credentials; it should normally remain local-only and must not cause filenames or content to be exposed in model prompts.”. The present recommendation is a shallow, user-approved professional-standing packet, with any member carrying third-party case material routed to protection instead. Held as prose: if fields ever land, the credential or the cycle would precede document function. Not time-first - “For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders.”.

collides_with.signal: THE unresolved overlap on this row, and it is recorded rather than smoothed over. Both situations hold an issuing body, a credential title, an identifier, and a validity window, and a clinician's registration certificate satisfies both descriptions exactly. The discriminating evidence this row claims: a requested-privileges or scope-of-practice list, a payer or panel enrolment designation, a revalidation cycle with required-evidence sections, or case-log evidence about patients - none of which a general professional licence carries. Where only a certificate exists, the two rows are NOT distinguishable and neither should win on that evidence alone. The memo files this as NJ-CP-2: whether this row should fold into career.credentials-licenses, or whether the credentialing WORKFLOW is the licence for a separate row. Provenance: inference.

Hospital privileging arrives through the same office and often in the same envelope as an employment offer. The discriminating evidence: a requested-privileges list, a scope of practice, or a primary-source-verification section supports this row; a job title, remuneration terms, and start-date conditions support employment records. A hospital name and a signature block support neither. Provenance: inference.

Continuing-education certificates are the same artifact from two angles: evidence a registration consumes, and a course completed. The discriminating evidence: an accrediting body plus a credit-type designation tied to a professional cycle supports this row; a school, a term, an instructor, or a course-code pattern with academic context supports the academic side. A certificate with a course title supports neither on its own. Provenance: inference.

A registration card pairs a person's name with an official number under an authority's seal, which is also the shape of an identity document, and credentialing bundles physically contain identity documents. The discriminating evidence: a document establishing WHO someone is, issued by a civil authority, is identity; a document establishing what someone may DO clinically, issued by a health regulator or a facility, is this row. A name beside a number and a seal discriminates neither. Provenance: inference.

falls_through_to.why: The home for a credential record carrying a verifiable identifier tied to a named person, and for any credentialing member carrying third-party case material. 00 names credentials in the definition itself: “Protected Records may represent sensitive isolated material such as passport scans, medical documents, account statements, visas, legal forms, or credentials; it should normally remain local-only and must not cause filenames or content to be exposed in model prompts.”

The home for a standalone certificate or notice with a durable purpose and no cycle around it. “Independent Records may live under Personal/Independent Records and hold standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group.”

The home for an isolated renewal fee receipt or enrolment confirmation. “Receipts and Confirmations may hold isolated invoices, delivery confirmations, booking records, boarding passes, purchase receipts, event tickets, and similar transactional documents.”

The cautious outcome for a certificate-shaped document whose issuing body and credential kind stay unresolved. “Review Later may hold files whose meaning is partly understood but whose final location requires a future decision.”

The inactive home for regulator guidance, standards documents, and process explainers that are about credentialing rather than evidence of it. “Reading Inbox may hold papers, articles, reports, and saved PDFs that appear to be reading material but have no active research, course, or project association.”

The safe outcome for a password-protected portfolio archive or an unreadable credentialing export. “Unsupported or Encrypted may hold—or, more safely, represent without moving—password-protected archives, unreadable documents, damaged files, and unknown formats.”

sensitivity_why: 00 names this material directly, twice: the corpus “can include identity documents, account statements, tax records, medical information, legal records, credentials, private correspondence, GPS metadata, employment materials, and educational records.”, and the residual definition is written over “Protected Records may represent sensitive isolated material such as passport scans, medical documents, account statements, visas, legal forms, or credentials; it should normally remain local-only and must not cause filenames or content to be exposed in model prompts.”. Two aggravating factors are stated as inference, not as design claims: a registration document carries a registry-verifiable identifier tied to a named person, and a credentialing bundle routinely CONTAINS an identity document, a CV, references, disciplinary correspondence, and case logs about patients - so the packet is more sensitive than any of its ordinary members. This row assigns only the catalogue value potentially_sensitive; it does not assign, alias, rank, or infer a P7 handling class.
open_question: Recorded as NJ-CP-2 and it is a genuine fold question, not a formality. Should this row exist at all, or should clinician credentialing be a branch pattern on career.credentials-licenses? The argument FOR keeping it: the credentialing workflow (privileging, payer enrolment, revalidation cycles) has detection signals and privacy rules a general licence row does not have, and it is the only situation on this family where the holder's own professional evidence carries third-party case material - which is precisely why it sits on the clinical_practice schema. The argument AGAINST: on the single most common file, a certificate, the two rows are indistinguishable, and neither has any dimensions today because both schemas are field-less, so the node test's third leg cannot be satisfied by either. This row does not settle it and does not pretend the overlap is smaller than it is. A second, smaller fork: whether continuing-education material should sit here (as evidence a cycle consumes, which is how the legacy med.clinician-cme row was folded) or on academic.continuing-education.
